title: Absent keys with documented answers
question: Does a key left out of the simulator call act like a key absent from a real request? AWS says: "If you do not provide a value for a context key, the simulation still runs and returns an implicit deny." Each case's documented answer is something else.

cases.name: string_not_equals_on_an_absent_tag
cases.description: A negated operator holds when its key is missing.

documented.source: If the policy condition requires that the key is not matched, such as StringNotLike or ArnNotLike, and the right key is not present, the condition is true.

cases.name: string_like_if_exists_on_an_absent_instance_type
cases.description: The condition from AWS's StringLikeIfExists example, whose table says a request with no ec2:InstanceType is a match.

documented.source: If the key is not present, evaluate the condition element as true.

cases.name: null_true_on_an_absent_token_issue_time
cases.description: Null true holds when the key is missing, as for a request made with access keys.

documented.source: In the policy statement, use either true (the key doesn't exist — it is null) or false (the key exists and its value is not null).
